correctness.rationale: For n≥2, p>0 and a real symmetric traceless A, the ellipsoid radius obeys rho_K(u)=R(1+epsilon u^TAu)+O(epsilon²). With eta=R phi′(R)/phi(R), the conical measure has relative first variation (n+eta)q_A. In the exact Li–Liu–Huang characterization (1.10), the integrand variation is (2−p)q_B+(n+p+eta)q_A while the polar quadratic term varies as 2q_B. The normalized sphere moment n∫(x·u)²q_C(u)/|S|=(tr C+2q_C(x))/(n+2) yields trace(B)=0 and (n+p)B=(n+p+eta)A. The linearized ellipsoid equation has scalar eigenvalue p and traceless eigenvalue 2(n+p)/(n+2), both nonzero, so implicit differentiation is justified and global uniqueness identifies the branch. Gaussian phi′/phi=−R gives c_R=1−R²/(n+p). At the critical radius only the first derivative vanishes; no second-order theorem follows. This independently reconstructs all quantifiers, normalization and boundary restrictions; numerical stress tests are not the proof.

First-order zero at R=√(n+p) does not determine second-order sign.

value.rationale: The derivative gives an exact n,p-dependent Gaussian radius where the weighted dual John ellipsoid map loses and then reverses anisotropic response. This is an interpretable stability/bifurcation threshold for a natural affine-geometric optimizer, rather than a mere numerical instance or a tautological normalization. The radial log-density formula also isolates which one-jet of the measure determines local anisotropy. The critical second-order dynamics remain open.
residual_risks: Local to spheres and degree-two ellipsoidal paths, not global nonlinear ellipsoid classification.

limitations: Local first derivative only; no second-order behavior at critical Gaussian radius.
General positive locally C1 radial density, n≥2,p>0; no nonellipsoidal perturbations.
